page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The memory configuration consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB per vCPU. Cache resources include 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 33 MB L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across multi-core and memory bandwidth operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test yielded 7430.34, and the PassMark CPU score reached 8305.34, both falling into the average tier. Memory bandwidth is measured at 412.9 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 48.32 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is weak, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1138.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1409.67.

The primary tradeoff of the n2-highcpu-8 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio. With only 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, memory-intensive workloads will face constraints, as reflected in the weak PassMark memory score of 1328.72. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance provides a dense allocation of compute cores relative to memory, making it cost-effective for CPU-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints.

This server is suited for workloads such as software compilation, text processing, and static web serving, where it demonstrates average benchmark throughput. It is also capable of handling light LLM inference tasks, achieving 415.57 tokens/second for prompt processing on a small 135M parameter model. It is less suitable for memory-heavy databases, image processing, or complex physics simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor at 2.8 GHz. It contains 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, 33 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show average multi-core CPU performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 8305.34 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 7430.34. However, single-core performance and memory metrics are weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1138.0 and a PassMark memory score of 1328.72. This resource profile makes the server qualitatively cost-effective for compute-dense, low-memory tasks. It is best suited for workloads such as software compilation, text processing, static web serving, and small-scale language model inference.
